To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the twin kilohertz QPO frequencies observed in 4U 1636−53 can be explained by nonlinear resonance between two modes of oscillations of an accretion disk; 2) the modes are identified with those of the Papaloizou-Pringle type; 3) the frequencies of the modes are determined by the neutron star mass and radius; 4) the mass and radius of the star are consistent with those of the canonical neutron star; and

the observed twin kHz QPO frequencies in accreting millisecond pulsars can be explained by resonant oscillations in the accreted disk, and the neutron star spin frequency can be estimated with an accuracy of a few percent.

the twin kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (twin kilo-Hz QPOs) observed in the 2.5-ms X-ray pulsar 4U 1728-34 are likely caused by resonant oscillations in the accreted matter around the neutron star.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) The study of the properties of the accreted matter in the innermost regions of the accretions disks of X-ray pulsars, with the goal of understanding the mechanisms of the energy release in the neutron star surface.
the study of accreting neutron stars and black holes in X-ray binaries, with the emphasis on the physics of accretion disks and their interaction with neutron stars and black hole magnetospheres.
the study of the nonlinear dynamics of accretion disks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed twin kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4–3658, detected with the Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer, are due to the excitation of nonlinear resonances of the accreted matter in the inner part of the accretions disk.

the twin kilohertz QPOs in 4U 1608-52 are not the result of the beat between a high and low frequency mode, but that they are the result of the nonlinear resonance between the high and low frequency modes.
the observed QPOs can only be interpreted as resonances between the neutron star spin and the Keplerian frequency of the disk.

we have found that the two frequencies observed in the accreting pulsar SAXJ1808.4-3658 are in agreement with nonlinear resonance of oscillations of the disk around a rotating neutron star.
we have found a mechanism for generating the observed twin kilohertz quasar periodic oscillations in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4−3658.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the twin kilohertz QPOs observed in the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4−3658 can be explained by nonlinear resonances excited in the accre-tion disk around the rapidly rotating neutron star.
